title: DataBall must open many files into one session
lead: `Open` takes paths, directories and globs, with recursion on request, into one session. Every source is a row of a built-in `"source"` dimension (`_source_file`, `_source_hash`, `_source_type`, plus per-source metadata) that joins into `"data"`. This includes a single-file open, so hosts always see one shape. Schemas merge by name with numeric widening. The caller chooses whether a bad file aborts everything or is skipped and reported.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** Parquet views in a multi-source session (sources are copied in; db-09 views stay single-source); per-source transforms (db-13); join, dedupe and aggregate (db-14); CSV dialect handling (db-12); folding the overloads into one API (db-16); watch folders (non-goal).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Suite `docs/databall-v1.4-alignment.md`: hosts open one file, many files, or a recursive directory; "a run/source becomes a dimension in the layout (path, hash, detected type, per-source meta) that joins into the `"data"` view"; schema merge by default ("union by name, missing columns become null, widen numeric types (`INTEGER`→`BIGINT`→`DOUBLE`); any other conflict is an error"); for bad data "caller chooses: abort everything, or skip the bad file and report file / row / column / value".

Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec interview):

- Globs and directories use the BCL only: `Directory.EnumerateFiles` plus `System.IO.Enumeration.FileSystemName` for `*` and `?` in the last path segment, matched case-insensitively on every OS; `OpenOptions.Recursive` descends. No `**` inside paths and no new dependency.
- A built-in `"source"` dimension carries `_source_file`, `_source_hash` (SHA-256 hex), `_source_type` and per-source metadata keys as columns. `"meta"` keeps only values constant across all sources. A wide session (no `tables`) carries the lineage columns directly in `"data"`.
- Every file-opened session has the lineage, even with one file (one shape for hosts). Sessions built with `AddRow` and no file source have none; their rows get NULL lineage if a file is imported later.
- Widening in a layout session `ALTER`s the owning physical column (`ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE`) inside the import transaction, the same rule as a wide session.

From earlier reviews (notes on this item):

- Each later file bringing a new per-source metadata key re-splits the whole session (cost ~ files × session size), so stage all sources first and split once.
- A declared key column that arrives as metadata (constant in file 1) throws `tables.X.key ... is not in the data` in `TableLayout.Build`.
- Layout types are fixed at first import (resolved above by widening).
- Native `.ball` import attaches outside the in-process open-file gate (`src/DataBall/DuckDbStore.cs:22-25`), and several stored `_databall` configs need a merge policy.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/DataBall/OpenOptions.cs` (new): `SchemaPath`, `Writable`, `Recursive`, `BadFilePolicy OnBadFile` (`Abort` default, `Skip`), `EngineOptions? Engine` (db-07).
- `src/DataBall/OpenReport.cs` (new): `Sources` (path, type, hash, rows), `Skipped` (path, message, and row, column and value when the error carries them), `Ignored` (files from a directory or glob that detect as none).
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.Open.cs`: `Open`/`OpenAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> inputs, OpenOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`; the single-path overloads call it. Expansion: an existing file is itself; a directory whose subdirectories are all `key=value` is one hive source; any other directory yields its files (recursive with `Recursive`); a glob is allowed in the last segment only (a wildcard elsewhere throws). The result is sorted by full path (ordinal) with duplicates removed; an empty result throws. An explicitly named file that detects as none fails under the bad-file policy; one from expansion goes to `Ignored`. Archives: each CSV entry is its own source, `_source_file` = `<archive>!<entry>`.
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.cs`: `public OpenReport? OpenReport`; staging every source, then one merge and one split for the whole open; `ImportAsync` adds a source row too; `Bounce` keeps the lineage columns (added to its keep list, `:338-341`).
- `src/DataBall/DuckDbStore.cs` / `DuckDbStore.Layout.cs`: per-source staging with `_source_key`; the schema merge (union by name, case-insensitive; NULL for missing; integer pair → the wider integer, integer with `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE` → `DOUBLE`; any other conflict throws naming the column, both types and both files); widening by `ALTER` on `"data"` or on the owning layout table, also on `ImportAsync` append (one rule, replacing the cast-to-existing-type in `AppendFromTable`, `:796`); the built-in `source` dimension (keyed by `_source_file` + `_source_hash`) in layout sessions; per-source metadata reconciliation (a value equal across sources stays in `"meta"`; one that differs becomes a `source` column, backfilled from `"meta"` for earlier sources); config metadata extraction never removes a declared key column. Native `.ball` sources are attached through the open-file gate (refused while that path is open writable in-process) and detached after staging. Their stored configs: the first `.ball` (when no schema is given) is the baseline, and later ones merge `Columns`, `Relationships` and `Metadata`; a different `tables` throws.
- `src/DataBall/Config.cs`: reserve the table name `source` and names starting `_source`.
- `src/DataBall.Cli/CommandFactory.cs`: `import` takes several inputs plus `--recursive` and `--skip-bad`.
- `README.md` ("Library usage", "Tables", "CLI") and `docs/how-it-works.md`.
- Tests: new `tests/DataBall.Tests/MultiFileOpenTests.cs`; existing tests whose expected columns or CSV output change gain the lineage columns; CLI import tests.
- No new dependencies (SHA-256 via `System.Security.Cryptography`).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `MultiFileOpenTests` unless noted; each asserts:

1. `Open_TwoCsv_OneSession`: the row count is the sum; each row's `_source_file` is its file; `_source_hash` equals the file's SHA-256.
2. `Open_SingleCsv_HasLineage`.
3. `Open_Directory_RecursiveOrNot`.
4. `Open_Glob_LastSegment_CaseInsensitive`; `Open_Glob_InDirectorySegment_Throws`.
5. `Open_Directory_UnknownFilesIgnored`; `Open_ExplicitUnknownFile_Fails`.
6. `Open_SchemaMerge_UnionByName_NullForMissing`.
7. `Open_SchemaMerge_Widens` (theory over wide and layout sessions): INTEGER then BIGINT then DOUBLE; the owning physical column's type in `information_schema.columns`.
8. `Open_SchemaMerge_VarcharVsDouble_Throws`: the message names the column, both types and both files.
9. `Open_PerSourceMetadata`: a differing value is a `source` column; an equal value stays in `Metadata`.
10. `Open_DeclaredKeyArrivesConstant_DoesNotThrow`.
11. `Open_TwentyFiles_NewMetaKeyEach_SplitsOnce`: an internal split counter is 1.
12. `Open_BadFile_Abort`: throws naming the file; no session; no path left in the open-file gate.
13. `Open_BadFile_Skip`: the other files land; `OpenReport.Skipped` names the bad one. `Open_AllBad_Skip_Throws`.
14. `Open_Archive_EachEntryIsASource`.
15. `Open_TwoBalls_ConfigsMerge`; `Open_TwoBalls_DifferentTables_Throws`; `Open_Ball_OpenWritableInProcess_Throws`.
16. `Bounce_KeepsLineage`.
17. `ImportAsync_Append_AddsSourceAndWidens`.
18. `Open_SingleParquetView_HasLineage`: the db-09 view carries constant lineage columns.
19. `Config_ReservedSourceNames_Rejected` (`ConfigTests`).
20. CLI: `Import_ManyInputs_Recursive_SkipBad`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `slicer start db-11 --render --strict`. Write tests 1–20; run them and record each red line.
2. `OpenOptions`, `OpenReport`, expansion and sorting.
3. Per-source staging with lineage; the schema merge and widening (wide, then layout `ALTER`).
4. The `source` dimension and metadata reconciliation; stage all, then split once; the declared-key fix.
5. The bad-file policy; native `.ball` sources through the gate and the config merge.
6. `ImportAsync` lineage and widening; `Bounce` keep list; CLI.
7. Update the existing tests whose expected shape now includes lineage, listing each changed assertion in the handoff note.
8. README and `docs/how-it-works.md`.
9. Mutation-check every new test; full Release test run; `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format DataBall.sln --verify-no-changes`
- CLI smoke: `databall import <dir> --recursive -o s.ball`, then `databall query s.ball "SELECT _source_file, count(*) FROM data GROUP BY 1"`.
- `slicer check`

sections.body: One DataBall commit on branch `db-11` (worktree `.worktrees/db-11`), merged to `main` after the gate and the owner's go-ahead.
